title: Security-gate rollout needs enumerator coverage, scope-source parity, and emit completeness
summary: Landing an io-layer gate is only half the work — every enumerator must adopt the bound-partition probe via a shared helper (not per-site fallbacks), the binding must come from resolveProjectScope (env + scope.env + execution scope), and dist checks need completeness alongside freshness.
procedure_steps: (1) When a protected prefix starts denying enumeration, find every enumerator (grep safeReaddir/safeLstat over the prefix) — the ones bypassing the shared scan break silently or crash sweeps; consolidate behind one helper (missionTierScanDirs). (2) Identity binding has three sources (env, persisted scope.env, execution scope) — a check that reads only process.env misses scope.env-bound daemons; always resolve via the same resolver the io layer uses. (3) Denial asymmetry: existsSync reads as false while lstat/readdir throw — enumerators must treat invisible and missing the same at tier roots. (4) Freshness and completeness are different axes for dist: incremental tsc can credit un-emitted outputs; verify recorded sources have their expected .js (emit_missing). (5) A third copy of a fallback is the signal to centralize — the per-site try/probe pattern drifted before the shared helper landed.
safety_notes: Require approval before irreversible or high-risk actions.
Capture evidence before and after the action.
escalation_conditions: Result does not match the expected state
